correctness.rationale: Reconstructed all three similarity classes. A nonscalar repeated-eigenvalue matrix has rank-one square-zero part with range equal to kernel; an orthonormal basis puts this part in the form with single positive entry equal to its norm. In the distinct-eigenvalue case the normalized involution Q satisfies QQ*=(Q*Q)^(-1); for norm a>1 it takes the right singular line of singular value a to the orthogonal right singular line of singular value 1/a. Fixing the phase gives the canonical entries a and 1/a. For a=1, Q is a selfadjoint unitary involution with eigenvalues ±1, and the sum/difference basis gives the same form. Thus the diagonal map diag(b/a,1) in the A-to-B orientation intertwines both canonical families with condition number max(a/b,b/a). Apply the affine polynomial defining the nilpotent or involution to any amplified intertwiner and use norm preservation under tensoring with a nonzero Hilbert identity to obtain the reverse bound in both directions. Tensoring the optimal small intertwiner gives equality and attainment for arbitrary nonzero K, including nonseparable K. The scalar case is identity; choosing involutions of norms 1 and t with spectrum {±1} gives the envelope theta_(2,q)(t)=t, including t=1. Replay: these identities and RESULT.md Steps 1–5; verify.py and VERIFICATION.md inspected, not executed. The finite assertions are not evidence for arbitrary amplification on their own.
